text:
Maya (she/her): FYI — during the Saturday deploy we triggered a cross-region failover that sent a lot of EU traffic to us-west. Seeing NAT SNAT exhaustion and LB 502s.
Sam: ugh. any idea what kicked the failover? GeoDNS health checks?
Maya (she/her): Looks like Route53 latency-based routing fell back when our eu-west ALB health checks flaked for ~90s. TTL is 300s so a lot of clients re-resolved to us-west.
Jonah: we also had sticky sessions on the ALB and a couple of services rely on connection affinity, so once they hit us-west they kept opening new connections -> SNAT table growth.
Li: ops-bot posted alerts about NAT gateway SNAT exhaustion at 02:12 UTC: `NAT-gtw-eu-01 SNAT table full` then return 502s on inference edge nodes.
ops-bot: ALERT: region=eu-west alert=natsnat_exhausted instance=NAT-gtw-eu-01 count=1 start=2024-07-20T02:12:31Z
Sam: Can you paste the health-check config? I want to check thresholds and path.
Maya (she/her): health-checks were basic /_hc (200), 2 attempts, 10s timeout, 2 failed -> unhealthy. Route53 config: latency-based, failover on health. TTL 300.
Maya (she/her): quick `dig` we ran:```
;; WHEN: Sat Jul 20 02:13:12 UTC
;; ANSWER SECTION:
service.redwood.example. 300 IN A 3.234.12.45 ; us-west
```
Sam: TTL=300 explains the blast radius. We should lower to 30s for all inference endpoints or use health-based weighted routing with fast failover.
Nadia: lowering TTL has cost/route churn implications and increases DNS queries. cost note: estimate +12% to Route53 queries. Worth it for Prod SLOs.
Jonah: short-term mitigation: 1) reduce TTL to 30 for critical endpoints, 2) increase ALB health-check attempts/timeouts to avoid flapping, 3) pre-warm additional NAT capacity or switch to EFA-backed egress nodes.
Li: long-term: add connection draining + region pinning flag for tenants who require strict affinity. Also implement egress per-az auto-scale to avoid single NAT bottleneck.
Sam: Also consider making GeoDNS fallback prefer same-region standby IPs with weighted health checks instead of sending to far region. Priority list: same-region fallback -> nearby region -> global.
Maya (she/her): Agreed. I'll update the runbook with failover policy: TTL 30, health-checks 3 attempts 5s timeout, Route53 weighted failover with health checks, and a sticky-cookie opt-out for cross-region rebinds.
Maya (she/her): Action owners: @Sam handle Route53/DNS config, @Jonah handle NAT capacity + egress autoscale, @Li prototype region-pin flag, @Nadia confirm cost impact and approvals.
Sam: I'll push a quick change to lower TTL to 30 for the inference zone in a canary first (eu-west only).
Jonah: I'll scale NAT pool and add a saturation alarm threshold + runbook step to swap in spare NAT.
Nadia: I'll model the Route53 query cost and get approval for the 12% increase on prod only.
Li: For region-pin, suggestion: metadata on tenant -> prefer region pinning via sticky header and enforce at edge LB. Adds complexity but solves noisy-neighbor cross-region storms.
Maya (she/her): One more note: check client-side resolver behavior — mobile clients sometimes cache beyond TTL. We'll add a doc note to customer-facing status pages.
Sam: can we also add a small change to the traffic router to respect `X-Region-Pref` header when present? That buys us per-tenant pinning without DNS churn.
Jonah: yes, we can respect header and set L7 routing. Need to make sure signature/proof of origin so clients can't spoof.
Maya (she/her): Good call. I'll open tickets and tag owners.
Sam: thanks — setting calendar follow-up for Monday 10:00 UTC to verify fixes. :thumbsup:
Maya (she/her): Thanks everyone.
